overview: Auntea Jenny is a fast-growing, franchise-led, multi-brand freshly-made tea and beverage company based in Shanghai, operating primarily under the Auntea Jenny (滬上阿姨) and Fallstea (茶瀑布) brands (with Jenny x Coffee as a smaller third brand). The company holds a strong position among mid-priced, freshly-made tea shop brands in China's lower-tier ('sinking') markets, competing in the same mass-market tea category as Mixue, Guming (Cha Panda), Chagee and Mixue. It listed on the HKEX Main Board on 8 May 2025 and reports in RMB while trading in HKD.

business_model.summary: Revenue is earned almost entirely from a franchise/wholesale model: the company sells ingredients, packaging and equipment to franchisees and collects franchise/operation service fees tied to franchisee purchasing volume, rather than from royalties on franchisee store sales directly. Franchisees fund store leases, staffing and day-to-day operations; the company supplies site-selection support, a standardized digitalized store management system, training, R&D/new products, and a nationwide supply chain/cold-chain logistics network. Revenue is therefore largely transactional (tied to product shipments to franchisees) and scales with store count and franchisee order volume rather than being a classic recurring royalty stream.

revenue_streams.name: Sale of goods to franchisees (ingredients, packaging, equipment)
Franchise service fees (training, marketing, digital/operations support)

business_model.customer_type: B2B (franchisees) funding B2C tea-shop operations; ~8,014 franchisees operating 13,120 franchised stores as of H1 FY2026
business_model.geographic_mix: Overwhelmingly mainland China (over 300 cities, all 4 municipalities, 5 autonomous regions, 22 provinces), with nascent overseas expansion: 61 overseas stores by H1 FY2026 (up from 45 at FY2025 and 1 a year earlier), newly entering the UK, Australia and Indonesia in H1 FY2026, alongside existing US, South Korea and Malaysia presence. Over half of stores (53.4% at H1 FY2026) are in third-tier-and-below cities, the company's core focus.

main_competitors: Mixue Ice Cream & Tea (蜜雪冰城)
competitive_position.market_position: A 'second-tier' challenger by scale in China's freshly-made tea category -- ranked around 4th nationally by store count per CIC/third-party data as of recent years -- well behind market leader Mixue (c. 46,000+ stores) and behind Guming, but ahead of smaller regional chains. Positioned in the mid-price, mass-market/lower-tier-city segment, directly overlapping with Mixue's core turf, which commentators describe as a disadvantage in brand differentiation versus Mixue's scale and Guming's density.

moat_factors.description: 13,000+ store network generates bargaining power for raw material procurement; direct-sourcing partnerships with origin suppliers/OEMs; 16 large warehousing/logistics bases, 11 frontline cold-chain warehouses, and a Haiyan (Zhejiang) production facility for tapioca pearls, taro products and tea leaves.

moat_factors.factor: Franchise network density in lower-tier cities
moat_factors.description: Deliberate focus on third-tier-and-below cities (53%+ of stores), the largest and fastest-growing segment of China's tea market per CIC; store coverage advantage in markets less contested by premium brands.

154 million WeChat mini-program registered members, 17.4 million average quarterly active members, 42.5% quarterly repurchase rate (FY2025) -- respectable but brand is widely viewed as less differentiated than Mixue or Chagee.

Auntea Jenny (mainstream/health positioning), Fallstea (value, 'real tea real milk'), and Jenny x Coffee allow segmentation across price points and tea/coffee convergence, but none has the singular brand recognition of top-tier peers.

weaknesses: Widely characterized by analysts as a 'second-tier' player lacking the brand recognition/differentiation of Mixue or the premium cachet of Chagee/Heytea
Heavy exposure to the most commoditized, price-competitive segment of the tea category (mass-market, lower-tier cities), where product differentiation is limited
Franchise store closure rate has been elevated (2025 full-year closure rate cited around 12%; partially improved in H1 2026) -- indicates franchisee unit economics / churn risk
Very low self-operated store count (35 of 13,155) limits direct visibility/control over the in-store customer experience and brand consistency
Short public trading history (listed May 2025) with thin analyst coverage and a small free float, contributing to high share price volatility

growth_drivers: Store network expansion: franchised stores grew from 9,152 (FY2024) to 11,423 (FY2025) to 13,120 (H1 FY2026) -- total network of 13,155 stores at H1 FY2026, up from 9,436 a year earlier (+39% YoY); management explicitly accelerated store-opening pace in H2 2025 and continued into H1 2026
Franchisee base growth: 6,974 franchisees (FY2025) to 8,014 franchisees (H1 FY2026), supporting continued unit growth and providing a franchisee-funded capital-light expansion model
Deepening penetration of third-tier-and-below cities, the largest and (per CIC) fastest-growing segment of China's freshly-made tea market through 2028

International expansion: overseas stores grew from 1 (H1 FY2025) to 45 (FY2025) to 61 (H1 FY2026), newly entering the UK, Australia and Indonesia in H1 FY2026, alongside the US, South Korea and Malaysia

Product innovation and tea-coffee convergence: 213 new products launched in FY2025, 142 in H1 FY2026 alone; rollout of coffee machines/coffee category expansion to broaden consumption occasions and lift store productivity
'Daily Health+' positioning (kale/fruit-vegetable tea lines) differentiating on health perception versus sugary mass-market peers
Supply chain upgrades (expanding cold-chain network, direct-sourcing/OEM partnerships) to support continued scale-driven cost advantages and margin stability as volumes grow
Improving store closure/churn metrics in H1 2026 versus H1 2025, suggesting better franchisee unit economics as the network matures

business.risk: Intense competition in mass-market tea category
business.description: Direct competition with much larger-scale Mixue and densely-networked Guming in the same lower-tier city segment; industry overall revenue growth has slowed sharply (cited ~9% vs 20-30% historically) as the market matures/consolidates and total shop count has started shrinking nationally despite continued openings

business.risk: Franchise model execution and store closures
business.description: FY2025 franchise store closure count rose to 1,383 (from 987 in FY2024); elevated closure rate (cited ~12% in FY2025) reflects franchisees unable to run stores profitably or losing lease renewals; franchisee quality control and support is central to the business but outside direct operational control

Characterized by some analysts as a 'second-tier' brand without Mixue's scale cost advantage or Chagee's premium brand equity, making it vulnerable to share loss in a saturating, price-sensitive category
Industry-wide food safety scares can hurt the company even when not at fault, given reliance on franchisee execution across 13,000+ independently-run outlets

business.risk: Fraud/misconduct by franchisees, employees or third parties
business.description: Disclosed as a principal risk factor; company cannot guarantee detection/prevention of all such instances across a large franchise network

financial.description: IPO proceeds received in HKD while operations are RMB-denominated; growing overseas operations (US, Korea, Malaysia, UK, Australia, Indonesia) add further multi-currency exposure; company does not hedge FX

financial.risk: Rising dividend payout ratio vs. cash needs
financial.description: Interim dividend payout ratio rose to ~65.5% in H1 FY2026 from ~35% a year earlier -- a shareholder-friendly signal but reduces cash retained for supply chain/overseas investment if growth capex needs increase
Disclosed risk around ability to fulfill obligations tied to contract liabilities (advance payments from franchisees for goods/equipment), which could affect liquidity/reputation if unmet

regulatory.description: Business permits, licenses and approvals required for franchise operations, manufacturing, food safety, environmental/fire-safety compliance; loss or delay of any could materially hurt operations

regulatory.risk: Online/offline payment and data privacy regulation
regulatory.description: Exposure to tightening PRC rules on third-party payment platforms, online transactions, and data privacy/security compliance

regulatory.risk: Expiry of preferential tax treatment and government grants
regulatory.description: Company currently benefits from certain PRC government grants and preferential tax treatments that could be withdrawn or changed
Subject to CSRC and other PRC authority approval/filing requirements for future fundraising, which could constrain capital flexibility

macro.description: Explicitly disclosed as a principal risk ('macro-economic factors have had and may continue to have a material adverse effect'); freshly-made tea is a discretionary, small-ticket impulse purchase highly sensitive to consumer confidence and disposable income trends in China, particularly in lower-tier cities

Nationwide tea shop count reported to have fallen net (~39,000 net decline despite ~118,000 openings in the trailing year per Canyan Data) as of mid-2025, signaling a maturing, increasingly zero-sum market
Exposure to tea leaf, dairy, fruit and packaging costs; scale procurement provides some buffer but commodity price swings could compress franchisee and company margins

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's freshly-made tea/coffee market has decelerated from 20-30% historical growth to roughly single-digit growth industry-wide as of 2025-2026, with the overall market estimated at RMB 354.7 billion in 2024 (+6.4% YoY, per iiMedia) and total store count nationally contracting net despite continued new openings -- a sign of consolidation around scale leaders (Mixue) and differentiated premium players (Chagee, Heytea). Third-tier-and-below cities remain the largest and (per CIC) fastest-growing sub-segment through 2028, which is Auntea Jenny's core focus.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate -- small-ticket discretionary consumer spending on beverages is more resilient than big-ticket discretionary categories but still sensitive to consumer confidence, especially among lower-tier-city and younger consumers who are Auntea Jenny's core demographic
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low -- company carries minimal debt (RMB2.0 million bank borrowings at FY2025, down from RMB29.9 million) and net cash position (~RMB1.35 billion cash and time deposits at FY2025), limiting direct interest rate exposure
key_input_costs: Tapioca pearls/taro (partly self-manufactured at Haiyan facility)

recent_developments.event: Stock remains well below its 2026 highs; 52-week range cited around HK$73.5-182.7, with shares roughly halved from IPO-era peaks amid broader volatility in China consumer/tea-sector names

Shares fell 23.4% in a single day (largest one-day drop since listing), erasing roughly HK$2.9 billion of market cap, following an announcement the prior evening on voluntary extension of pre-IPO shareholder lock-ups -- market read the notice negatively despite management framing it as a confidence signal. Six shareholders could sell up to ~3.5% of total share capital between 7 Aug and 7 Nov 2026; five others (including Shanghai Puhai Enterprise Management) pledged not to sell before 7 Nov 2026

H1 FY2026 interim results: revenue +42.4% YoY to RMB2.589 billion, net profit +58.3% YoY to RMB321 million, adjusted net profit +41.6% YoY to RMB345 million; gross margin stable at ~31.6%; store network reached 13,155 (13,120 franchised); interim dividend of RMB2.00/share, raising the payout ratio to ~65.5% from ~35% a year earlier
Pre-IPO shareholders, including the controlling shareholder, announced voluntary extension of lock-up periods by three to six months ahead of the original 7 May 2026 lock-up expiry
Analyst consensus revenue/EPS forecasts for FY2026 were raised, though the consensus price target was cut ~8% to around HK$103, reflecting multiple compression even as estimates improved
GF Securities initiated coverage with a Buy rating and HK$121.32 fair value (18x FY2026 P/E); Haitong International initiated with Outperform and a HK$105 target (16x FY2026 P/E)

Listed on the HKEX Main Board, raising gross proceeds of approximately HK$273 million (net ~HK$195 million), with intended use split roughly 25% digital capabilities, 20% R&D, 20% supply chain, 15% brand/store network expansion, 10% marketing

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Interim Results (31 July / 28 August 2026)

items.target: Continued orderly, quality-first expansion focused on lower-tier cities
items.notes: No specific numeric store-count target disclosed; management states intent to 'scientifically screen regional presence grids' and expand 'in an orderly manner' while prioritizing single-store profitability and shortening franchisee payback periods. H1 2026 already added 1,697 net new stores.
Explicit 2026 outlook priority ('Channel Diversification: Expanding stores in an orderly manner, and improving single-store profitability') but no quantified target disclosed.

items.target: Accelerate coffee rollout and tea-coffee integration
items.notes: Qualitative target to broaden consumption scenarios via coffee machines/new coffee SKUs; no numeric target given.

items.target: Continue international expansion into new markets
items.notes: Grew from 45 overseas stores (FY2025) to 61 (H1 FY2026), newly entering UK, Australia and Indonesia; no specific overseas store count target disclosed for year-end.
Up from ~35% in H1 FY2025, signaling confidence in cash generation, though no explicit forward payout policy was quantified for FY2026 full year.

guidance.management_commentary: Management's FY2025 outlook (reiterated into H1 FY2026) centers on five pillars: (1) orderly store network expansion with improved single-store profitability and shorter franchisee payback periods; (2) product innovation tracking consumption trends and accelerating tea-coffee convergence; (3) supply chain upgrades (logistics network, cold-chain coverage, bargaining power with suppliers); (4) differentiated multi-brand strategy to penetrate different market segments; and (5) deeper digitalization across the full business process, including food-safety control. Management highlighted that H1 2026 franchised-store closures decreased year-on-year even as openings accelerated, citing this as evidence of 'synergistic development of scale expansion and operational efficiency.' No formal quantitative revenue/profit guidance range for FY2026 was identified in the filings reviewed.

bull_case: Rapid, capital-light store network growth funded by franchisees -- store count up ~39% YoY to 13,155 at H1 FY2026, with revenue +42.4% and net profit +58.3% YoY in the same period, demonstrating strong operating leverage
Deep, defensible focus on China's largest and fastest-growing tea sub-segment (third-tier-and-below cities), an area less contested by premium brands like Chagee/Heytea

Net cash balance sheet (~RMB1.35bn cash/deposits vs. only RMB2.0m bank debt at FY2025) gives balance sheet flexibility to fund supply chain investment and overseas expansion without dilution or leverage
Early-stage but broadening overseas expansion (UK, Australia, Indonesia added in H1 2026 alongside US/Korea/Malaysia) offers a long-dated optionality growth vector beyond the maturing domestic market

Improving franchise unit economics signaled by declining store closure counts in H1 2026 even as new-store openings accelerated, and a near-doubling of the interim dividend payout ratio reflecting management confidence in cash generation
bear_case: Positioned as a 'second-tier' brand in an intensely competitive, saturating mass-market tea category dominated by much larger-scale Mixue and densely-networked Guming, with limited brand differentiation or pricing power

Industry-wide deceleration -- national tea shop count reportedly shrinking net despite continued openings, and sector revenue growth slowing to single digits from historical 20-30% rates -- raises risk that store growth cannibalizes same-system sales or runs into diminishing returns

Franchise churn risk: FY2025 saw 1,383 franchised stores close (up from 987 in FY2024), an elevated closure rate reflecting franchisee profitability challenges that could worsen in a softer Chinese consumer spending environment

August 2026 lock-up-extension episode (23% single-day share price drop) highlights thin float, concentrated pre-IPO shareholder base, high stock volatility, and potential overhang risk as extended lock-ups eventually expire

Entirely RMB-reporting/mainland-China-dependent earnings base (overseas still <1% of stores) leaves the company highly exposed to China consumer discretionary spending softness, with no FX hedging in place despite a dual-currency (RMB operations / HKD-raised capital) structure
